answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable bond and emit a regular heartbeat pulse proving it completed verifiable work, not just claimed it. New identities start with a whisper of trust and must mirror the behaviour of proven agents over many rounds before earning full privileges, so a flood of cheap copies cannot instantly vote, trade, or claim rewards. An attacker must therefore fund and maintain each fake for a long time, making mass fakery far more expensive than honest participation.
